label: One front camera
description: One inexpensive camera recessed into the front of the body. Turn the robot to inspect an area before moving into it.
capability: Live video, object recognition and visual landmarks.
limitation: One image does not directly measure distance in metres. The sides and rear are outside the view.
algorithmBody: Stream selected camera frames to the Mac mini or cloud vision model for object and room understanding. Run visual landmarks and monocular SLAM on the mini; calibrated wheel motion or a measured marker supplies a metric reference.
mappingBody: Start with known landmarks and short supervised moves. General room navigation needs calibrated visual mapping and a measured scale; a language model looking at a picture does not provide a distance map.

label: Front + left + right
description: Three inexpensive cameras inside the body: one looking forward and two angled 45° left and right. Their views overlap ahead of the robot.
capability: Overlapping front and forward-side views for object recognition and visual checks before moving.
limitation: Forward coverage is roughly a half-circle, not 360°. The rear remains unseen. Independent cameras do not provide synchronized stereo depth.
algorithmBody: Stream labeled front and ±45° views to the Mac mini or cloud vision model. The mini handles geometric tracking and camera calibration. These inexpensive cameras capture images; they do not detect objects or run AI.
mappingBody: Run front-camera monocular tracking first, with scale tied to calibrated motion or a measured marker. Extra views can supply object context. Multi-camera SLAM and dense reconstruction are separate integration tasks.

label: Stereo camera pair
description: Two forward-facing cameras on one rigid board, recessed inside the body. Synchronized images and a calibrated baseline let software estimate distance.
capability: Front-facing stereo vision with a known baseline for metric depth after calibration.
limitation: Depth is computed on the Mac mini. Glass, blank surfaces, poor light and occlusion can leave gaps.
algorithmBody: Stream synchronized image pairs to the Mac mini. It calibrates and rectifies the views, then computes disparity with OpenCV StereoSGBM or RTAB-Map. With focal length f and baseline B, distance is Z = f × B / disparity.
mappingBody: The Mac mini runs RTAB-Map and navigation after stereo calibration. Invalid depth stays unknown. Vision LLMs on the mini or in the cloud interpret objects and rooms from selected images and map context.
